rows.description: A friend hears the same story reversed each time, with the partner always right and the person always confused. Outsiders often see the pattern before the person inside it does.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A person writes down dates and events privately, talks to a trusted friend or counsellor, and checks their perception with someone outside. Reality is protected by other anchors than the person casting doubt.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A person goes silent after a disagreement, expecting the other to plead and give in. The silence is a way to feel powerful when words feel risky, but it punishes rather than protects.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26

rows.description: The person receiving the silence feels dread, replays what they did, and hurries to apologise for anything. Being ignored activates real social pain, which makes this tactic effective and cruel.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: fear, anxiety, detachment, hurt

rows.subtype: Asking for a pause versus stonewalling [Response]
rows.description: A mature person says I need an hour to calm down and will come back, which is a break with a promise to return. Punishing silence has no end date and demands surrender.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.description: A teenager or adult complains about one person to another to gain allies, or carries messages that stir jealousy. Direct talk feels risky, so a third party becomes a shield or a weapon.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Being compared or used as a go-between [Receiver]
rows.description: A person is told a partner's ex is better, or a parent uses the child to pass hurtful messages to the other parent. It creates anxiety, divided loyalty and a sense of never being safe.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: anxiety, trust, hurt

rows.description: A person who hears gossip or is asked to carry messages suggests the two talk directly and declines to take sides. Refusing to be a channel keeps relationships cleaner.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A person always presents themselves as wronged, so any complaint against them turns into sympathy for themselves. Behind it is often a fragile self-image that cannot tolerate being at fault.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26

rows.description: A teenager who owns a mistake with a plain sorry finds that relationships recover faster than through defensiveness. Taking responsibility is strength, and it does not mean accepting all blame.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
